issues.legal_issue: A tenant who remains in possession after a lease expires does not become a contractual tenant holding over merely because the landlord accepts rent while statutory protection prevents eviction.
material_facts: The lease was for a fixed term and expired by efflux of time.
The tenant remained in possession under the protection of rent-restriction legislation.
The landlord accepted rent after expiry, but there was no other evidence that the landlord assented to continued possession or intended to renew the lease.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was a statutory tenant, not a tenant holding over under a renewed lease; acceptance of rent alone did not establish renewal.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 111(a) and 116 of the Transfer of Property Act, a lease for a fixed term determines by efflux of time, and holding over requires the landlord’s assent to continued possession. Where rent-restriction legislation protects the tenant after expiry, acceptance of rent alone does not manifest that assent. The Court followed Kai Khushroo Bezonjee Capadia v. Bai Jerbai Hirjibhoy Warden and relied on Ganga Dutt Murarka v. Kartik Chandra Das and Bhawanji Lakhamshi v. Himatlal Jamnadas Dani.

rule.if: post_expiry_tenancy_status_dispute and fixed_term_lease_expired and tenant_remained_under_rent_protection and rent_acceptance_was_only_evidence_of_assent

predicates.post_expiry_tenancy_status_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a tenant’s possession after expiry of a lease is contractual or protected by rent-restriction legislation.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired: The tenant’s fixed-term lease ended and the tenant did not leave at its expiry.
predicates.tenant_remained_under_rent_protection: The tenant remained in possession under statutory protection against eviction.
predicates.rent_acceptance_was_only_evidence_of_ass: The landlord accepted rent after expiry, but there was no other evidence that the landlord assented to continued possession or intended to renew the lease.

issues.definition: If a fixed-term lease has expired, the tenant remains under rent protection, and acceptance of rent is the only evidence of the landlord’s assent, the tenancy is not contractually renewed.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory tenant whose lease has already determined need not receive a fresh notice to quit before an ejectment action is brought under rent-restriction legislation.
material_facts: The lease expired by efflux of time, and the tenant continued in possession as a statutory tenant.
The landlord commenced an ejectment action under rent-restriction legislation without serving a notice to quit.
The tenant argued that the action was not maintainable without notice.
issues.conclusion: A fresh notice to quit was not required, and the ejectment action was maintainable without one.
issues.legal_principle: Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act concerns termination of a subsisting contractual tenancy by notice; under section 111, a lease may determine by efflux of time or another prescribed mode. Once the lease has determined, the contract has ended, so no further notice is needed to terminate it. The Court followed Kai Khushroo Bezonjee Capadia v. Bai Jerbai Hirjibhoy Warden and affirmed Ganga Dutt Murarka v. Kartik Chandra Das, Bhawanji Lakhamshi v. Himatlal Jamnadas Dani, and Bhaiya Ram v. Mahavir Prasad. It distinguished Mangilal v. Suganchand Rathi, Manujendra Dutt v. Purendu Prosad Roy Chowdhury, and Rawal & Co. v. K. C. Ramachandran, and overruled Lalitha v. Avisumma.

rule.if: rent_act_ejectment_proceeding and lease_already_determined and tenant_remained_as_statutory_tenant and tenant_claimed_notice_was_required

predicates.rent_act_ejectment_proceeding: The landlord brought an ejectment proceeding under legislation protecting tenants from eviction except on specified grounds.
predicates.lease_already_determined: The contractual lease had ended before the ejectment proceeding began.
predicates.tenant_remained_as_statutory_tenant: The tenant remained in possession after the lease ended under statutory protection against eviction.
predicates.tenant_claimed_notice_was_required: The tenant contended that the landlord had to give a notice to quit before bringing the ejectment proceeding.

issues.definition: When an ejectment proceeding is brought under tenant-protection legislation against a tenant whose lease has already ended and who remains only as a statutory tenant, a fresh notice to quit is not required.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent, evidence-supported findings that a building is unsafe and unfit for human habitation are not displaced merely because it has remained standing and in use during prolonged litigation.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the building was dilapidated and unsafe for human habitation.
After remand, the lower courts concurrently found that the building was in a dilapidated condition and unfit for human habitation.
The evidence included an eastern wall that was out of plumb and an uneven roof, neither of which could be properly repaired without the tenant vacating.
The tenant had made minor repairs, and the building remained standing and in use during the prolonged litigation.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s contention did not warrant re-examination of the factual findings; the eviction decree was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal by special leave, the Supreme Court ordinarily does not re-examine concurrent factual findings supported by evidence. Continued occupation and minor repairs do not negate supported findings that a building is unsafe and unfit for human habitation. The eviction action was under section 13 of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act, 1949; no earlier case was cited for this point.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_ejectment_decr: The case is an appeal by special leave from a decree ordering eviction on a building-condition ground.
predicates.concurrent_findings_building_unsafe: The courts below made concurrent findings that the building was dilapidated, unsafe, or unfit for human habitation.
predicates.findings_supported_by_evidence: Evidence supported the findings, including defects that could not be properly repaired without the tenant vacating.
predicates.tenant_relied_on_continued_use_or_minor_: The tenant relied on continued use of the building or repairs made by the tenant to dispute the findings.

issues.definition: Where an appeal by special leave challenges an eviction decree, concurrent evidence-supported findings of unsafe building conditions are upheld despite the tenant’s reliance on continued use or minor repairs.
